reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural number J>=2 and every real h>0, take the J zero-based indices Fin(J)={0,...,J-1}. Define
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi))
for each i in Fin(J), where i and J are cast exactly to real numbers and the denominator J-1 is real subtraction after casting J. For each j in Fin(J), let ell_j be the actual real Lagrange cardinal polynomial for these nodes,
  ell_j(X)=product_{i in Fin(J),i!=j} (X-t_i)/(t_j-t_i).
Then for every j in Fin(J),
  0 <= integral_0^h ell_j(s) ds.
The integral is the oriented interval integral against ordinary real Lebesgue measure; because h>0 it has the usual increasing endpoints 0 and h. It is not a probability integral or a trigonometric weighted integral. Polynomial continuity supplies integrability internally, rather than through an extra hypothesis. The conclusion includes both endpoint indices j=0 and j=J-1, as well as every interior index when present.
The assertion is nonnegativity of each signed basis integral. It does not assert strict positivity of the integral, pointwise nonnegativity of ell_j(s), a normalization identity for the total weights, a bound on interpolation growth, or any probability-kernel or algorithmic-cost result. No additional cardinality, positivity-of-coefficients or integrator premise is supplied.

Each integral is a finite real scalar. No ambient vector space,probability measure,gradient or kernel appears.

Both endpoint indices are included. There are no existential nodes,coefficient arrays or polynomial witnesses,no parity restriction on J and no omitted endpoint exception.

No extra positive-coefficient,positive-integral,cardinal-formula,regularity or integrability premise is assumed;the actual polynomial structure supplies the relevant continuity/integrability.
